grand_strategy.reading: Brunei is a small, rich sultanate whose economy rests on one resource, oil and gas, with LNG sold to Japan since 1972. Its strategy is defensive and borrowed: it keeps its Islamic-monarchic identity at home (the 2014 sharia penal code, stoning in force since 2019), buys its security abroad (a British garrison and Singapore's jungle camp), and buys diversification from outside (Hengyi, Chinese capital at Pulau Muara Besar). The sharia code is the price it has chosen to pay for legitimacy, and the boycott it drew is the cost. The Limbang claim against Malaysia stays dormant rather than pressed.

stances.note: Partner through the 2009 settlement of the Kikeh and maritime boundary dispute, with the Limbang claim left dormant: Malaysian press reported in March 2009 that Brunei had dropped it; Brunei denied this and said the Limbang question was never discussed in the exchange of letters. Dormant, not withdrawn. Bond kin is our reading of the shared Malay identity and language; no cited source calls it kinship.

stances.note: Transactional: the Hengyi refinery at Pulau Muara Besar, 70% Zhejiang Hengyi and 30% Damai Holdings (a subsidiary of the state's Strategic Development Capital Fund, Wikipedia pointer). Phase 1 cost US$3.445bn and reached full operation in November 2019; Phase 2 launched in January 2026 on a US$13.6bn package. Brunei-Guangxi Economic Corridor (2014, about US$500m pledged) is a second layer. Brunei holds a Spratly claim (Wikipedia pointer), but no source yet describes its posture toward China's claim, so none is written. 2024-25 contacts not verified. Bond none.
